key_insight: Deep backward multistep high-order regression (MHDBR) combines BSDE representations and neural regression to solve high-dimensional semilinear parabolic PDEs with a decomposed error bound.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a framework for balancing time discretization, conditional Monte Carlo sampling, and network approximation in high-dimensional PDE solvers.
method: Represent the PDE through a backward stochastic differential equation.
Combine multistep time discretization with conditional-expectation regression targets.
For gradient-independent generators, obtain order J in nodal L² error using constrained GroupSort networks and sufficiently large conditional samples.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes a reproducible time-discretization test satisfying the analytical assumptions and three broader neural-network benchmarks whose alignment with those assumptions is discussed.
watch_item: The theory assumes exact population minimization, excludes finite-training-sample generalization and optimization errors, and does not establish dimension-independent complexity.
paper_title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations
